personal.name: Alsahid Simms
personal.summary: Backend engineer building secure Java and Spring Boot services for fintech, government and law enforcement, including Verification of Payee fraud prevention and the National Crime Agency's digital evidence platform. Owns services end to end, from turning vague requirements into a defined backlog through to design, delivery and debugging. Recent work centres on event-driven systems on AWS SNS/SQS: idempotent dispatch, race-condition fixes, and hardening third-party integrations against credential leaks.
personal.intro: A disciplined, security-minded engineer who architects defensive, event-driven systems for regulated sectors, from vetting platforms to financial infrastructure, and drives technical design decisions from concept to production.

highlights: Backend engineer on a pre-launch programme replacing a legacy vetting and background-check platform, owning the Communication service end to end and supporting the wider platform. Turned vague requirements into a defined backlog, driving client questions via the Business Analyst and authoring tickets, including a document-upload track the team built.

Automated Notifications & Reminders: Built the platform's automated notification capability: an event-driven delivery framework across on-system and email channels, with a unique claim preventing double sends, rendering first so a failed render never blocks the event, and a configurable per-condition reminder-threshold model built on the same idempotent-dispatch discipline.

Scheduled Bulk Email Delivery: Built scheduled bulk email delivery with idempotent per-recipient dispatch and mid-batch cancellation. Found and fixed two dispatch bugs: a crash-interrupted row that silently skipped its recipient on every retry, fixed by telling a crashed row apart from a completed one, and a cancel/complete race that could flip a cancelled send back to completed, fixed with an atomic conditional database update.

Third-Party Integration Security: Caught and fixed a credential leak before merge, where following a redirect from the platform's screening provider (Fama) would have sent internal API credentials to an unauthenticated, external S3 link. Disabled automatic redirects, then pre-emptively applied the same defensive principle (never send this credential to an unrelated host) to the e-signature integration (Signable).

Compliance Evidence Coverage: Resolved a gap where check reports were stored only on the webhook-triggered completion path, leaving providers that complete exclusively via polling, including the screening provider (Fama), with no retrievable evidence at all. Consolidated storage into a single completion listener shared across both paths, with retry-safe handling for failed downloads.

Cloud Storage Architecture: Designed a direct-to-S3 storage layer across two microservices: presigned-URL uploads for applicant documents and server-side storage for raw third-party check reports, with a write-then-verify model that confirms each upload against S3 rather than trusting client-reported success. Built the S3 service layer and document data model for applicant documents.

Technical Design Authorship: Authored the technical specification for a document-management epic spanning two microservices, defining RBAC-scoped API contracts, a deterministic S3 key structure, and encryption at rest. Also proposed the design for a cross-service communications and notifications system spanning 11 tickets and three microservices, identifying race conditions, missing duplicate-prevention safeguards, and data model gaps before implementation began.
Core Engineering Team engineer on the platform's foundational services, enforcing security and PSD2 compliance for a system serving 2,000+ financial institutions.

Fraud Prevention (VoP): Built features for the Verification of Payee (VoP) service, a payee verification layer that combats authorised push payment fraud, mandated under the EU Instant Payments Regulation (Oct 2025). Implemented strict IBAN validation and regex-based character normalisation to resolve naming discrepancies.

Microservices Resilience: Improved fault tolerance for downstream dependencies by implementing exponential backoff for transient outages, nearly eliminating client-reported false failures on the VoP service. Enforced an error masking strategy that maps internal failures (500) to generic dependency errors (424), preventing the accidental exposure of backend infrastructure details.

Scalability & Performance: Took end-to-end ownership of a performance risk flagged by the Tech Lead: proposed and implemented cursor-based pagination, dynamic filtering, and database indexing on core endpoints, preventing a latency outage before onboarding larger enterprise clients.

Observability & Production Debugging: Used Grafana telemetry to visualise inter-service interactions and resolve production bugs, with K8s port forwarding for local cluster access and debugging. Deployed via ArgoCD and Kubernetes for safe, incremental rollouts, with Docker for containerisation.

Access Control: Implemented scope-based access control using JWTs to unify authorisation across internal infrastructure and external Open Banking services, enforcing per-client permissions and tenant data isolation.
Built Spring Boot microservices for the National Crime Agency's digital evidence platform, later taking ownership of the legacy Java 6 monolith.

Microservices & API Development: Collaborated within a 5-person team to develop the digital evidence capture REST APIs, documenting contracts with Swagger. Used Spring Boot Actuator for observability and took ownership of the auditing Non-Functional Requirement, extending pre-existing Spring AOP pointcuts to capture custom 'during-execution' states for a fine-grained digital evidence audit trail.

Concurrent Engineering & Quality: Expanded scope to engineer new features across a dual-stack architecture, working across Java 8 microservices and the legacy Java 6 monolith. Maintained 85% test coverage across unit and integration tests, tracked in SonarQube.
Mentoring: Mentored two junior developers through pair programming and architectural reviews, including a frontend developer moving into backend.
Product Impact: Influenced a product decision to replace rigid postcode matching with fuzzy matching, clearing an evidence submission backlog for officers and removing manual postcode verification.

Legacy Modernisation: Owned the legacy monolith's side of the team's strangler-fig integration, then modernised one of its components as sole engineer over three months, using feature flags for safe, controlled rollouts. Managed database schema migrations across three dependent projects and led PI planning sessions with the Product Owner and Test Manager to define technical roadmaps.
Refactored legacy REST APIs and resolved bugs for the County Court digital filing system (HM Courts & Tribunals Service), maintaining 80% test coverage with JaCoCo throughout the modernisation.
Promoted from Associate to Senior Software Engineer based on delivery excellence across Government and Investment Banking sectors.

Senior Software Engineer (Jun 2021 – Sep 2021): Built a Function-as-a-Service solution in Node.js using AWS SAM for the DWP's SMS notification service. Led the migration of legacy XML APIs to RESTful standards, writing data migration scripts for PostgreSQL.

Analyst Software Engineer (Dec 2019 – Jun 2021): Delivered full-stack Scala (Play Framework) microservices on GOV.UK for the HMRC National Duty Repayment Centre, meeting the Government Design Standard and integrating with Pega workflow systems.

Earlier roles (Jun 2017 – Dec 2019): Associate Software Engineer maintaining Home Office reporting systems (Oracle Middleware, BI Publisher) and directing a testing team of 6 on a BAE Systems defence programme, supporting Java microservices for the UBS eFX trading platform.
